TextView.android:text:
What is SpeechBridge? A learning and practice app connected to an engineering research project. It can show measurements from phone recordings.

Who is it for? It is being developed for guided phonation practice in the context of post-stroke dysarthria. It is not a validated clinical system.

What is dysarthria? A speech difficulty related to how the nervous system controls speaking muscles.

Why practise phonation? Phonation means making voice. Some app exercises let you practise a comfortable voice sound and review its recording.

Why use an accelerometer? A future sensor on the neck could detect vibration where it touches the skin. It does not directly measure vocal-fold movement, and it is not connected yet.

Why use EMG? Surface EMG uses skin electrodes to record small electrical signals from muscles beneath them. It does not directly measure vocal-fold muscle activity, and it is not connected yet.

Why is a microphone needed? The phone microphone records sound. The app uses that recording to estimate sound activity and signal features.

Why plan to use more than one sensor? Each sensor detects a different kind of signal. The project is investigating whether extra information is useful; more sensors do not guarantee better feedback.

What is the ESP32-S3? A small controller planned for collecting readings from the future wearable. It is not connected in this app version.

What is BLE? Bluetooth Low Energy, a way devices can send small amounts of information wirelessly. Wearable data is not being sent in this version.

Do I need a wearable? No. The learning screens and phone-microphone practice can be used without one. Wearable readings are unavailable.

What if a sensor disconnects? The app should identify the reading as unavailable, not invent a value. No wearable connection is implemented here.

What is a personal baseline? An earlier measurement from your own similar exercise, used only for context. It is not a target or medical standard.

What do results mean? They are estimates from a prototype recording and can be affected by the room, phone, and recording quality.

Can SpeechBridge diagnose dysarthria? No.

Can it replace a speech-language therapist? No. It cannot provide personal assessment or treatment.

Is SpeechBridge clinically validated? No. It is an engineering research prototype, not a clinically validated medical device.
